# 1 Kings Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** About that time, Jeroboam's son Abijah became ill.
**2** Jeroboam told his wife, "Disguise yourself so no one will recognize you as my wife, and go to Shiloh. The prophet Ahijah is there — the one who told me I would become king.
**3** Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey with you. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
**4** Jeroboam's wife did as he said. She went to Shiloh and came to Ahijah's house. Ahijah was old and had lost his sight.
**5** But the LORD had told Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her sick son. I will tell you what to say to her. When she arrives, she will be pretending to be someone else."
**6** So when Ahijah heard her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you pretending? I have bad news for you.
**7** Go tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I raised you up from among the people and made you leader over my people Israel.
**8** I tore the kingdom away from David's house and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commands and followed me with his whole heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
**9** Instead, you have done more evil than anyone before you. You have made other gods for yourself — metal idols — provoking me to anger. You have thrown me behind your back.
**10** Because of this, I am going to bring disaster on your house. I will wipe out every male in your family line — slave or free — in Israel. I will burn your dynasty the way someone burns dung, until nothing is left.
**11** Dogs will eat any of your family who die in the city, and vultures will eat any who die in the countryside. The LORD has spoken.'
**12** As for you — go home. The moment you set foot in the city, the boy will die.
**13** All Israel will mourn for him and give him a proper burial. He is the only one of Jeroboam's family who will be buried, because he is the only one in whom the LORD found something good.
**14** The LORD will raise up a king over Israel who will destroy the house of Jeroboam. This begins today — right now.
**15** The LORD will strike Israel until it sways like a reed in water. He will uproot Israel from this good land he gave their ancestors and scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they set up Asherah poles and provoked the LORD.
**16** He will give up on Israel because of the sins Jeroboam committed and led Israel into."
**17** Jeroboam's wife got up and left. When she arrived at Tirzah and stepped across the threshold of her house, the boy died.
**18** All Israel buried him and mourned for him, just as the LORD had said through his servant, the prophet Ahijah.
**19** The rest of Jeroboam's reign — his wars and how he ruled — is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
**20** Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years. Then he died, and his son Nadab succeeded him.
**21** Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon was ruling in Judah. He was forty-one when he became king and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem — the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel as the place for his name. His mother's name was Naamah; she was an Ammonite.
**22** Judah did evil in the LORD's eyes. Their sins made him jealous — sins worse than anything their ancestors had committed.
**23** They too built high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every hilltop and under every leafy tree.
**24** There were even male cult prostitutes in the land. The people practiced all the disgusting customs of the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel.
**25** In the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
**26** He carried off the treasures of the LORD's temple and the royal palace — everything. He took all of Solomon's gold shields.
**27** King Rehoboam replaced them with bronze shields, which he entrusted to the commanders of his palace guard.
**28** Whenever the king went to the LORD's temple, the guards carried the shields, then returned them to the guardroom.
**29** The rest of Rehoboam's reign and everything he did is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
**30** Rehoboam and Jeroboam were continually at war.
**31** Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His mother was Naamah the Ammonite. His son Abijam succeeded him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **14:6 — "Why are you pretending?"**: The blind prophet sees through the disguise. Ahijah's physical blindness only heightens his spiritual perception — a contrast with Jeroboam, who has perfect eyesight and sees nothing of spiritual reality.
2. **14:9 — "thrown me behind your back"**: God speaks as someone personally rejected — not just disobeyed, but discarded like something worthless. This is the language of a relationship betrayed, not merely a law broken.
3. **14:13 — "the only one"**: In a dynasty of evil, one child has something good in him. He alone gets a funeral. The cruel mercy of this passage is that his death saves him from watching what happens to the rest of the family.
4. **14:27 — bronze for gold**: One image captures the entire story of the divided kingdom. What Solomon built in gold, Rehoboam replaces with bronze. The kingdom's decline is visible in the material of its shields.

— PNEUMA
